title: What Happens If You Jump Into Ice Water
youtubeTitle: What Happens If You Jump Into Ice Water?
description: What cold water does to your body in the first few minutes.

characters.name: Sam
characters.look: a man in his 20s, short black hair, red hoodie, blue jeans, white sneakers

scenes.narration: What happens if you jump into a frozen lake in the middle of winter?
scenes.visual: Sam stands at the edge of a frozen lake in the snow

scenes.narration: In the first second, the cold hits your skin like a wall.
scenes.visual: Sam plunges into icy water, splash

scenes.narration: You gasp without meaning to, and that gasp can pull water into your lungs.
scenes.visual: Sam gasps in the water, close-up

scenes.narration: Your heart races, and your breathing jumps to four times its normal speed.
This is cold shock, and it is the most dangerous part.
If you stay calm for one minute, your breathing slows back down.
Then you have about ten minutes before your arms and legs stop working.
scenes.visual: Sam swimming slowly toward the shore

scenes.narration: Your body pulls warm blood away from your hands to protect your heart.
scenes.visual: Sam's hands on the ice edge

scenes.narration: That is why your fingers go numb first.
Back on the shore, you are still in danger.
scenes.visual: Sam climbs out onto the snow

scenes.narration: Cold blood from your legs rushes back to your heart and can chill it.
So the safest move is to get warm slowly, not to jump into a hot bath.
scenes.visual: Sam by a warm fire in a cabin
